newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Chief Minister of India's West bengal state, Jyoti Basu, is scheduled to arrive here on November 27 on a five-day visit to Bangladesh. The visit is considered crucial in shoring up the proposed water sharing agreement between Dhaka and New Delhi.

The opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has lodged a formal complaint with the Speaker that the party was not consulted before announcing two parliamentary standing committees during the last session of parliament.
A meeting of the National Economic Council on Saturday reviewed the implementation status of the Annual Development Programme (ADP) under the fourth Five-year Plan.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria has said that intending entrepreneurs would not be asked to furnish the source of their capital and no levy would be imposed on setting up industries in the country.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has suggested that the poor people be provided with jobs or some sort of work instead of helping them with cash.
Post and Telecommunication Minister Mohammad Nasim has said that the government is trying hard to ensure education for all by the years 2000.

The U.N. Development Programme (UNDP) may withdraw its financial and other supports to the project known as Support for Strengthening Parliamentary Democray following the opposition BNP's decision not to involve with a Task force headed by Speaker Humayun Rashid Choudhury.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was Saturday apprised of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, a project conceived way back in 1961. The project has yet to be implemented.
